Jacob (ACME): Hey team — we've been seeing intermittent 503s and truncated streaming responses from the hosted inference endpoint when using the Python SDK (v2.4.1). Happens mostly during ramped traffic (~200 rps), roughly 1-3% of requests. Example error from our client:

```
  requests.exceptions.HTTPError: 503 Server Error: Service Unavailable for url: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  ...
  http2: STREAM_ERROR (REFUSED_STREAM) id=12345
```

Repro steps we've used: long-lived HTTP/2 connection with multiplexing enabled (session pool size 4), sending streaming completions concurrently (multiple streams per connection). Root request id we captured: req-0a1b2c3d.

Anyone seen this pattern before? We can provide pcap/logs if helpful.

Amy (Support): Thanks @Jacob, sorry about the disruption — we'll investigate. Can you paste the raw request id (you gave one, thx) and a short curl that reproduces the issue? Also: are you using the SDK default http2 multiplexing or did you enable a custom pool/adapter? Any retry/backoff config?

Jacob (ACME): Curl we used to reproduce (non-deterministic but shows 503s occasionally):

```
curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-mini","input":"stream test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```

We're on the Python SDK with connection pool size=4, multiplexing enabled (default), and an internal short backoff (exp backoff starting at 200ms). We see the 503 come back very quickly for some requests, sometimes after a few KB of stream data.

Dan (Oncall): @Maya can you take a look? Tagging since this smells like gateway http2 stream resets / envoys hitting stream concurrency limits. Quick workaround for the customer: try adding header `X-Disable-Multiplex: 1` to force single stream per connection or reduce concurrent streams in the client.

Maya (SRE): looking... I pulled gateway logs for the customer's IP and req-0a1b2c3d. There's a small spike in `REFUSED_STREAM` / `STREAM_RESET` around those timestamps. Snippet from gateway logs (redacted):

```
[2026-08-12T14:22:31Z] proxyd gateway-node-5 incoming conn ip=1.2.3.4 req=req-0a1b2c3d level=error msg="stream reset: REFUSED_STREAM"
[2026-08-12T14:22:31Z] proxyd upstream error upstream=worker-a code=503 details="upstream reset while streaming"
```

Rate calc: customer IP saw ~1.7% 503s over a 30m window, but gateway-node-group-b as a whole had a smaller uptick. Hypothesis: under high multiplexed concurrent streams, we occasionally exceed an internal concurrency handling path in our ingress proxy which leads to stream resets (Envoy/our filters). There was a known issue where a combination of aggressive keepalive + high concurrent streams could trigger premature resets.

Immediate actions we recommend to customer as a workaround:
- Add header `X-Disable-Multiplex: 1` (temporary) or configure SDK to use fewer concurrent streams per connection (pool size 1-2)
- Add/ensure exponential client backoff on 5xx and REFUSED_STREAM, e.g., initial 300ms jittered

Repro steps we used internally:
```
# single-process repro (uses curl --http2)
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
    -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"model":"gpt-4-mini","input":"x"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream &
done
wait
# watch for REFUSED_STREAM / 503 in gateway logs
```

I'll schedule a rolling restart of gateway-node-group-b to clear any stuck state and also open a ticket to patch the concurrency check in the proxy.

Jacob (ACME): I added `X-Disable-Multiplex: 1` to our client and reran the load test — noticeably fewer 503s (was ~1.8%, now down to ~0.2%). Still see rare failures though. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Maya (SRE): good, that matches the hypothesis. Deploy-bot: scheduled rolling restart for gateway-node-group-b at 02:15 UTC — low-risk restart of N=6 nodes, staggered. :gear: 

deploy-bot: Rolling restart scheduled by Maya (SRE) for gateway-node-group-b at 2026-08-12T02:15:00Z. Nodes will be restarted one-at-a-time, health checks in place.

Maya (SRE): Next steps:
- Rolling restart will remove transient state; monitoring for regressions for 1h post-restart
- Patch branch prepared to harden stream concurrency handling in our ingress filter (PR #3372). We'll aim to ship the patch to staging tomorrow and to prod in the next maintenance window.
- SDK team: plan a micro release (v2.4.2) with a default tweak to reduce max concurrent streams and improved retry handling for REFUSED_STREAM and early 5xx on streaming.

Amy (Support): Drafting customer update: "Hi Jacob — we've identified a gateway-level edge case interacting with HTTP/2 multiplexing that can cause intermittent stream resets leading to 503s on streaming requests. Temporary workaround: add header `X-Disable-Multiplex: 1` or set SDK connection pool to 1-2. We're performing a rolling restart and will ship a fix in a near-term SDK/runtime release. We recommend upgrading to 2.4.2 when available. Apologies for the disruption; we'll keep you posted." OK to send? :pray: 

Jacob (ACME): Yes please send — that matches what we saw. Thanks everyone. We'll keep multiplex disabled for now and roll to 2.4.2 when out.

Dan (Oncall): Created incident ticket INC-2026-3487, priority P3, status: monitoring. Root cause: ingress HTTP/2 stream concurrency edge-case causing REFUSED_STREAM / early upstream 503s. Workarounds and mitigations documented. Will update after patch verification and SDK release. :white_check_mark:
